problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{z}}^{{e}^{z}}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{p}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{q}{\int }_{r}^{1}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$
worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(x)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,z)}^{{u}_{4}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{z}\le x\le {e}^{z},\,\,{z}^{2}-1\le y\le x+z}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{z}}^{{e}^{z}}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(x)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/41b06d98498273a03b9df8eeaa60f4e74cb00168e8dd0b3b395c5b0a23518e57.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\sqrt{z}\le x\le {e}^{z}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/07a37b90df8b37d07c40af03ecba8e665797cfff368758db7ae17e45f11683cf.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ are

$\,$ $z=0\,$ and $\,z={x}^{2}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ are

$\,$ $z=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,$ and $\,z=1.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,z)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡x\le z\le 1}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}^{1}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
